summary: Candidate research only; no dataset was downloaded or acquired. The strongest local lead is RWJUH New Brunswick’s linked machine-readable pricing file. CMS describes hospital standard charges and insurer Transparency in Coverage files that may complement it. The reviewed pages did not establish actual RWJUH or Saint Peter’s payments, patient responsibility, or a Middlesex County payment dataset. Keep each amount type and its rate or payment period distinct.

sources.title: Charges | RWJ University Hospital New Brunswick
sources.geography: RWJUH New Brunswick, Middlesex County, New Jersey; the linked file’s facility coverage requires verification
sources.period: The page says charge data is updated annually but gives no observed effective date for the linked file
sources.grain: Hospital item/service or DRG charge; payer, plan, setting, and rate-period grain in the linked file are unverified
useful_fields: plan and payer identifiers if present
observed_facts: The official hospital page links to a machine-readable file and a shoppable services file.
The page says its charges are updated annually and warns that chargemaster values do not establish an individual patient’s liability.
The page says the displayed discounted cash price may represent the estimated gross charge rather than the patient-specific discount.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the official page’s machine-readable-file link; record the resolved URL, file format, declared facility identity, version/effective date, size, and any redistribution terms. If those checks pass, acquire only a named service or code slice for RWJUH New Brunswick and one identified payer/plan, retaining the original record and source hash. Do not infer patient share from charges.
limitations: The external file URL and its metadata were not opened in this bounded review, so direct download URL, precise schema, facility scope, file size, rate period, and redistribution rights remain unverified.
Published standard charges and negotiated rates are not actual payments, allowed amounts, or patient responsibility.
No Saint Peter’s prices were inspected.

sources.title: Use of Pricing Information Published under the Transparency in Coverage Final Rule
sources.geography: Plan- and issuer-specific coverage; New Jersey applicability depends on locating the relevant issuer files
sources.period: Files are required from July 1, 2022 onward; individual file/rate periods must be read from each issuer’s data
sources.grain: In-network rate by plan/provider/service where represented; out-of-network allowed amounts and historical billed charges are also required file categories
observed_facts: CMS says most group health plans and issuers must make public machine-readable files for in-network rates and out-of-network allowed amounts and historical billed charges.
CMS says the Departments do not publish these files; plans and issuers host them on their own websites.
CMS notes that file size and complexity may require specific technology.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For one named New Jersey plan/issuer, locate its official transparency page and identify its in-network file. Check file size and schema before downloading; filter to RWJUH CCN 310038 or a matching verified provider identifier and one selected service/code. Preserve plan, provider, code, rate type, and effective period. Treat this as negotiated/allowed-rate evidence, not proof of a claim payment.
limitations: No specific insurer file or direct data URL was identified in this review.
Hospital inclusion and provider identifiers may be incomplete or ambiguous; validate facility and code mapping before use.
Rates do not establish utilization, actual paid amounts, or patient liability.

sources.title: Basic Stand Alone (BSA) Medicare Claims Public Use Files (PUFs)
sources.geography: National Medicare public-use files; local New Brunswick or Middlesex applicability is unverified
sources.period: Claim-type-specific periods; the page reviewed did not establish a current year suitable for the requested local comparison
sources.grain: De-identified claim-specific records; exact claim type, fields, and facility geography depend on individual file documentation
useful_fields: service or diagnosis/procedure coding fields as available
observed_facts: CMS describes these as free CSV downloads containing de-identified claim-specific information and states that they are public domain.
CMS says each file has its own documentation and warns that variables may be removed or recoded to protect beneficiary confidentiality.
The reviewed CMS page did not show a current facility-level download link or prove that providers remain identifiable.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Inspect the documentation for a relevant inpatient claim PUF and confirm whether it retains facility-level identifiers and separate payment fields. Proceed only if it supports the intended comparison; otherwise use the already identified provider-level Medicare DRG data for facility amounts and do not attribute national de-identified claims to these hospitals.
limitations: National/de-identified claim data may not support New Brunswick, facility, or Middlesex County estimates.
Availability of actual payment and patient-share fields at usable grain was not confirmed.
This source may duplicate or add little beyond the campaign’s existing Medicare 2024 DRG data.

missing_inputs: A verified RWJUH MRF URL, file size, file version/effective date, schema, and redistribution terms.
Equivalent official pricing file and scope confirmation for Saint Peter’s Medical Center CCN 310070.
A named insurer/plan file with verified inclusion of either local hospital and a bounded service slice.
Facility-level actual-payment and patient-responsibility data; the reviewed public sources do not establish those quantities locally.
simulation_use: Candidate inputs for a traceable price layer: keep gross charges, cash prices, payer-negotiated rates, out-of-network allowed amounts, Medicare payments, and patient responsibility in separate fields. Prefer a verified hospital file for local charges and negotiated rates, then link one verified insurer file by provider, code, plan, and period. Treat amounts as published rates unless a source explicitly reports claims payments. Do not use them to infer utilization or patient share.
limitations: This is discovery, not acquisition; no file contents, hashes, or dataset snapshots were inspected.
Only official primary-source pages were used. Page content is paraphrased.
National CMS materials are methodological or external benchmarks and are not substitutes for local facility payment evidence.
Access classification describes public page availability; direct machine-readable file access and reuse terms remain unverified.
